$readme: Manual analyst inputs for non-FCFF filer classes (utilities, banks, insurance, managed care). Each entry's `source` field must cite the regulatory order / 10-K page / CCAR disclosure the values came from. `as_of_date` should be ≤ 18 months old; the architecture-lock test flags stale entries. Add to this file via PR review — values directly drive intrinsic value for the listed ticker.

NEE.source: Florida PSC settlement approved 2025-11-20 (effective 2026-01-01 through 2029-12-31). Rate base $75.1B per FPL rate case filing for FY2026 projected test year (Feb 2025 filing). Rate-base growth derived from FY26→FY27 trajectory ($75.1B → $80.8B = 7.6%) corroborated by $21.7B 4-year capex plan. Allowed ROE 10.95% (band 9.95-11.95%) and 59.6% equity ratio are settlement-approved terms. NEER valued at 18x residual earnings (between yieldco ~13x and high-growth renewables developer ~22x; NEER is high-growth contracted generation).
NEE.analyst_notes: Sum-of-parts (Phase A.8): regulated FPL rate base + non-regulated NEER. FPL leg earns the 10.95% allowed ROE on the 59.6% equity-funded portion of the $75.1B rate base (NOT the full base). NEER leg = residual earnings (consolidated NI − FPL allowed equity earnings, which also nets holdco interest drag) × 18x. Two-stage FPL model: 4-year explicit period uses the FPSC-approved 7.5% rate-base growth; terminal reverts to GDP-level 2.5% as rate-base growth normalizes post-2029 capex spike. NEER ~30-40% of consolidated earnings; multiple is the key analyst lever — recalibrate vs renewables peer comps.

ET.source: Midstream MLP valuation. Headline: target EV/EBITDA 9.5x on stable fee-based EBITDA (peer set EPD ~10x, KMI ~9.5x, WMB ~10.5x, OKE ~10x; ET carries a modest complexity/governance discount). Distribution cross-check: ~$1.30/unit annualized distribution (2025 run-rate), ~3.5% target growth. Net debt ~$65B per latest balance sheet drives the EV->equity bridge.
ET.analyst_notes: FCFF mis-frames ET: ~$7B growth capex reads as value destruction and the ~$65B net debt is invisible until the EV->equity bridge. Headline is EV/EBITDA (equity = EBITDA x multiple - net debt, per unit); the EV/EBITDA multiple is the key analyst lever - recalibrate vs midstream peers. Distribution-discount leg (two-stage on DPU) is the income cross-check; DPU is an analyst input (distributions are not in the cleaned frame). Distribution-coverage check (DCF/distributions) deferred until the maintenance/growth capex split is extracted.

JPM.source: Q1 2026 declared quarterly dividend $1.50 ($6.00 annualized; 7.1% increase from $1.40). 29.16% payout ratio per company filings. 16 consecutive years of dividend increases. CCAR clearance + CEO Dimon commentary support continued ~7% growth trajectory. Ke override to 10% reflects bank-specific risk premium pure CAPM misses (regulatory capital + cyclical credit risk).
JPM.analyst_notes: Universal bank with bank-style income statement (no OperatingIncome line). Sustainable EPS growth ~7% reflects balance-sheet expansion + share buybacks. CEO succession risk (Dimon's tenure) is a discount factor not captured here; analysts may want to apply a -5-10% IV haircut.

AXP.source: Q2 2026 declared quarterly dividend $0.95 ($3.80 annualized; 16% increase from $0.82). 20.9% payout ratio. 5 consecutive years of increases. FY2026 EPS guidance $17.30-$17.90 supports double-digit growth.
AXP.analyst_notes: Closed-loop card issuer + consumer lending book. Low payout (20.9%) leaves substantial room for continued dividend growth. Higher beta than JPM (consumer-spending cycle exposure) handled via CAPM directly — no override.

UNH.source: TTM dividend $8.84 (Q1 2026 quarterly $2.21; ex-date June 16, 2026). 66.5% payout ratio. Annual 11%+ dividend growth trajectory historically. Managed care EPS growth ~11% sustained by Medicaid + Medicare expansion + Optum services.
UNH.analyst_notes: High payout (66.5%) caps near-term DPS growth at roughly Medicaid/Medicare reimbursement growth + buybacks. Float-based business; FCFF DCF doesn't apply because reserves + medical-cost trends distort operating cash flow. DOJ investigation (announced 2025) is a discount factor not captured here.

CNC.source: Two-stage residual income on normalized ROE. Normalized ROE 11% — through-cycle managed-care return between the depressed FY2026 (adj. EPS ~$3.40 ≈ 8% on current book) and the recovered FY2023-24 (10.5-12.5%); FY2025 GAAP ROE (−30%) is distorted by a large, non-recurring goodwill/intangible impairment and is NOT used. Ke 10% override — CNC's CAPM beta (~0.6) is stale (pre-collapse) and gives an implausible 6.2% Ke; 10% reflects the elevated risk of a distressed managed-care name (same rationale as the JPM bank override). Payout 30% proxies capital returned via buybacks (no dividend). Terminal growth 2.5% (GDP-level).
CNC.analyst_notes: CNC pays no dividend (DDM undefined) and FCFF overvalues ~7x (thin margin on ~$195B pass-through revenue + low WACC). Residual income on book + normalized ROE is the float-business frame. normalized_roe_pct is the key analyst lever — recalibrate vs through-cycle managed-care returns and cross-check the FY2025 impairment magnitude vs the 10-K. Book anchor is the post-impairment equity (the writedown is already reflected).

SOFI.source: PROVISIONAL — pending third-party validation. Two-stage residual income on a normalized ROE. normalized ROE 10% is a FORWARD/scaling assumption (current ~5%, FY2026; SOFI is ramping toward management's low-teens target) — NOT yet validated; this is the primary lever. No dividend (payout 0). Terminal growth 3% (growth fintech). Ke is CAPM with the live beta (~2.0 → ~13%); that beta is likely inflated by retail/meme volatility vs a ~1.3-1.5 fundamental, so the Ke is a SECOND lever to validate (a cost_of_equity_override_pct can dampen it).
SOFI.analyst_notes: SOFI digital bank/lender: DDM undefined (no dividend), FCFF wrong (negative FCF is loan-book growth, not distress). Residual income on book + normalized ROE. CAVEAT: residual income only adds value above book when ROE > Ke; at the current ~5% ROE vs ~13% CAPM Ke the IV is well below book. The result hinges entirely on (1) normalized_roe_pct and (2) the beta-driven Ke. Validate both vs third-party data (consensus ROE trajectory, a fundamental/peer beta) before trusting the IV.

BRK-B.source: Q1 2026 10-Q: BVPS $337.15 (Mar 31 2026). Insurance float $176.9B. Operating earnings Q1 2026 $9.6B. Historical 10-yr consolidated ROE ~10-12% (Buffett 2024 letter cites 11.4% average). Target P/B 1.4× reflects 10-year median market-implied premium-to-book (1.3-1.5× band). Ke override to 9% (vs pure CAPM ~7.5% from β 0.85) reflects insurance + sum-of-parts risk premium analysts apply.
BRK-B.analyst_notes: Simplified embedded-value framework: BVPS compounding × target P/B. Captures consolidated economics across insurance + BNSF + BHE + operating subsidiaries + ~$280B equity portfolio. Doesn't separately model float earnings (already embedded in ROE). Doesn't account for Apple position concentration risk (~25% of equity portfolio). For more granular sum-of-parts, Phase A.8 could decompose into: (a) insurance ANW, (b) operating subs DCF, (c) marketable equities at market.

EQIX.source: Equinix FY2025 10-K (period ended 2025-12-31): AFFO $3,761M / 98.1M diluted shares = $38.34/sh. Explicit AFFO/share growth 8% (low end of EQIX's stated 8-10% long-term AFFO/share growth algorithm); terminal growth 3% (data-center secular demand sustainably above ~2.5% nominal GDP). Ke via CAPM (no override).
EQIX.analyst_notes: Data-center equity REIT valued on a two-stage AFFO-growth model (the REIT analog of a DCF on free cash flow). AFFO is the REIT distributable-cash measure; FY2025 FFO was ~$2.78B and GAAP net income $1,350M — the FCFF engine is inappropriate here because RE depreciation depresses GAAP NI and the firm distributes most of its cash. Review AFFO/share + growth on the next 10-K.
